page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan. Left page: running head at top with page number at top left; one column of running text with a left margin note beside the line "bis injuriam facit"; no text below the main text. Right page: cropped at the gutter, showing only the word-ends of its lines at the right edge; no legible text.

main_text.p: obligare Christianos Magistratus in utramvis par-tem : quin ut iplis liceat, pro arbitratu suo, & prout incolumitati & utilitati Reipublicæ videbi-tur expedire, eandem apud subditos suos fancire, vel non fancire.

XXXI. Dico Quarto, Legem Moralem, à Mose traditam, hoc est, Præcepta Decalogi, obligare omnes Christianos, pariter ac Judæos, ad eam obser-vandam. Et hoc quidem omnes, quod sciam, Protestantes uno ore confitentur : quod majorem no-bis injuriam facit Bellarminus, qui nos fingit in eBellarm. 4. de Justific. 5.ponere Christianam libertatem, ut nulli legi subjecti simus in Conscientia, Mofes autem cum suo Decalogo nihil ad nos pertineat. Viderit quomodo se calumnia liberet ; suofque (si nos in hac culpa) eodem crimine. Agitatur enim haec controversia inter suos Scholasticos, teneanturne Christiani Præceptis Decalogi, quatenus sunt declarativa Legis Naturæ tantum, an etiam quatenus sunt Mosi à Deo, Deíque jussu à Mose populo Dei tradita, & in sacros Codices relata : aliis utrumque affirmantibus, aliis è duobus alterum negantibus. Est & in nostris Ecclesiis eandem reperire hac de re sententiarum, (si tamen sententiarum, & non verborum potius) diversitatem. Cæterum cum illi inter se, & nos cum illis in eo quod rei caput est, haftenus confentiamus ; habere moralem legem earn, quæ à Mose tradita est in præcepti Decalogi continetur, vim obligandi nostras Christianorum conscientias : fortasse non est operæ pretium, unde illam obligandi vim obtineat, multum litigare. Consultius tamen mihi loqui videtur qui dicunt Legem illam Mosis non obligare Christianos formaliter & qua talis, hoc est quatenus à Mose tradita est ; sed tantum ratione materiæ, quatenus declarativa est legis Naturalis: proinde vim suam obligandi omnem non ab au-thoritate[?]

page.notes: The right page is cut off at the gutter; only word-ends are visible, so its lines are given as fragments marked [?] and not as full words. The final word of the left page is split across two lines ("au-" / "thoritate"); the completion is doubtful. The page number "o3" is printed in old-style figures and is read as 63 with [?]. The marginal note "5." beside "ponere" is read as part of the note "Bellarm. 4. de Justific. 5.", and "in e" at the line end is cut off by the scan edge, so it is marked as the likely start of "in ea". Long s is written as plain s in the running head and text.
